“Hah—!”

I race into the park without looking aside.

The magical energy leaking through the air is immense and profoundly ominous.

It is like heavy oil poured into a clear stream.

Even I can sense power this dense.

I do not mean her appearance or her flesh.

The woman in black is drinking the person within her—her mind, her memories, everything that makes her human.

The victim does not stir.

As life steadily drains from her skin, she appears to be transformed into a doll while still alive.

“Shinji, you—”

My mind is paralyzed.

I cannot comprehend the situation. I cannot make a rational judgment.

Why is he here? What is the book in his hand? How can he smile when a woman is dying before him?

Why—why is something so insane happening before my eyes—!?

“—Did you kill her?”

My hand clenches.

I do not even see the Servant standing before Shinji.

My mind freezes.

Something far stronger than I am stands directly before me—a Servant from whom I ought to flee with all my strength—yet I feel no threat from her whatsoever.

The reason within me that should feel it is coming apart.

A doll that will do nothing without an order from her owner—her Master.

But once the command is given, she is a demon that will kill without hesitation.

He offers his Servant no support.

Then was he, like me, simply chosen as a Master by chance—?

“Get up and fight, you corpse…! You’re not alive anyway, so what difference do wounds make!? God, stop wasting time, you piece of garbage…! You’ve humiliated me! This makes it look as though *I’m* the weak one!”

Shinji continues to berate Rider.

Perhaps unable to watch any longer—

Sparks fly.

…What a vicious cycle.

Rider’s body can no longer fight.

And still, Shinji’s order punishes her for being unable to stand. Her wound deepens, and Rider’s life rapidly slips away.

Rider responds to Shinji’s command.

—An order founded upon the certainty of her death compels Rider’s body to move.

Then—

“That is enough. It seems the treasure was wasted upon you after all, Shinji.”

The rasping voice of an old man interrupts.

ぼう、という音。
「え、え……！？ 本、本が燃える……！」
慎二の持つ本が燃えていく。
pages.jaRuby:

“Huh?”

A soft roar.

“Wh-What…!? The book—the book is burning…!”

The book in Shinji’s hands catches fire.

「なんで……！？ くそ、消えろ、消えろってば、なんで燃えてんだよコイツ！？」
必死に炎をはたくが間に合わない。

ライダーの姿も、跡形もなく消え去った。

pages.en:
“Why…!? Damn it, go out! I said go out! Why is this thing burning!?”

He desperately beats at the flames, but it is too late.

The book burns away without a trace, and at the same instant—

Rider, too, vanishes completely.

“…Dear me. I expected little from you, but not so little as this. Affection for my grandson moved me to grant you a chance, yet now I have no choice but to abandon you.”

Where had he been hiding until now?

The old man—Zouken Matou—emerges as though seeping from the darkness of the night.

pages.ja:
「お、お爺、さま？ いまのは、まさか」
「ワシ以外に誰がおるのだ馬鹿者。折角のサーヴァントを殺しかけおって。それでも我が血脈の後継者か」

pages.en:
“G-Grandfather? Did you just—?”

“Who else could it have been, fool? You nearly killed a perfectly valuable Servant. Can one such as you truly be the heir to my bloodline?”

pages.ja: 「……！ な、ならなんで邪魔したんだよ！ 勝てばいいんだろ勝てば！ 僕は間桐の後継ぎなんだ、こんな奴等に負けるなんて許されないって判ってたのに……！」
pages.jaRuby: 「……！ な、ならなんで邪魔したんだよ！ 勝てばいいんだろ勝てば！ 僕は間桐の後継ぎなんだ、こんな奴等に負けるなんて許されないって判ってたのに……！」
pages.en: “—! Th-Then why did you interfere!? All that matters is winning, right!? I’m the heir to the Matou! I knew I couldn’t let myself lose to people like these…!”

pages.en:
Shinji runs to the old man as though seeking salvation.

Having lost Rider and found Saber bearing down upon him, he must have no one else upon whom to rely.

But—

「……痴れ者め。おまえのような出来そこないに勝利など求めておらぬわ。その身に求めたモノはな、無力でありながらも挑む我らの誇りじゃ。
にも拘わらずこの体たらく。間桐の名に泥を塗りおって。まったく、親子共々一門の面汚しよな」

「……痴れ者め。おまえのような出来そこないに勝利など求めておらぬわ。その身に求めたモノはな、無力でありながらも挑む我らの誇りじゃ。

pages.en:
“…Imbecile. I never expected victory from a failure such as you. What I required was the pride to challenge the enemy despite your impotence.

“Instead, you have reduced yourself to this and dragged the Makiri name through the mud. Father and son alike—you are disgraces to our house.”

」

pages.en:
“What—you think I’m the same as my father—?”

“Fool. You are less than he was. Your incompetent father contrived to produce an even more hopeless defect.

“…I clung to one slender hope that even so you might suffice, but it ends here. You have allowed not only your blood, but your spirit, to rot.

“The Matou bloodline ends with you.”

…Sensing something ominous in his gaze, Saber retreats by the slightest step.

pages.en: “In that case, it seems I must die. Worthless though he may be, the boy is my own blood. I must preserve his life even at the cost of mine. Kakah—truly, affection for one’s kin can be fatal.”

Still crawling, Shinji drags himself away.

Nausea burns in my chest.

“—Saber, stand back. I know that old man. I need to speak with him.”

“You must not. This man is not human. There can be nothing to discuss and nothing you should hear.”

“Oh? Is that all? The answer hardly need be spoken. As you have just said, I was the one who selected Shinji as a Master. As you see, I retired from active duty long ago.

“Unable to fight myself, I yielded the grand stage to my grandson.”

“You transferred the position of Master—then that means…”

pages.ja:

pages.en:
“Indeed. You and he are alike, heir of Emiya.

“When I learned the Holy Grail would appear, I had my grandson contract with a Servant in my place. You, too, stand at the end of a bloodline devoted to the arcane.

“Surely you understand the heart of one who entrusts an impossible dream to his pupil.”

なら慎二は魔術を学んでいて、その家が魔道であるって言いたいのか、この爺さんは。

Ordinarily, Masters are mages.

Does the old man mean that Shinji has studied magecraft and the Matou household is a lineage of mages?
